principle.

Assertion (A): Both the nuclear fission of a heavy nucleus ( ) and the nuclear fusion of two light
nuclei ( ) result in the release of energy.
Reason (R): The binding energy per nucleon ( ) is maximum in the intermediate mass region (
). In both processes, the system transitions to a state of higher total binding energy, which
corresponds to a decrease in the total rest mass of the system.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) (A) is true but (R) is false
(b) (A) is false but (R) is true
(c) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(d) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding nuclear fission and fusion:
(I) Nuclear fusion requires extremely high temperature and pressure primarily to overcome the strong
Coulomb repulsion between the interacting nuclei.
(II) In a nuclear fission reactor, the primary function of a moderator is to absorb excess neutrons and thereby
control the rate of the chain reaction.
(III) The energy released per nucleon in the fusion of light nuclei is generally greater than the energy released
per nucleon in the fission of heavy nuclei.
(IV) Thermal neutrons, which are highly effective in inducing fission in , typically have kinetic energies
of the order of .
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) (I) and (III) only (b) (I), (II) and (III) only
(c) (II) and (IV) only (d) (III) and (IV) only

Maxwell-Boltzmann probability speed distribution curve shifts to a higher speed, and the maximum value of
the probability density is reduced by a factor of .

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the degrees of freedom and molar heat capacity of a diatomic
gas:
(I) At room temperature, a diatomic gas molecule has active degrees of freedom, consisting of
translational and rotational degrees of freedom.
(II) At high temperatures, the activation of a single one-dimensional vibrational mode adds exactly
additional degree of freedom to the molecule.
(III) The molar heat capacity at constant volume ( ) of a diatomic gas increases by when one
vibrational mode becomes fully active.
(IV) According to the law of equipartition of energy, each fully active one-dimensional vibrational mode
contributes to the average internal energy of a single molecule.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) (I), (II) and (IV) only (b) (I) and (IV) only
(c) (II) and (III) only (d) (I), (III) and (IV) only

An ideal gas is taken from an initial state to a final state with and ,
while kept in thermal contact with a heat reservoir at a constant temperature . This transition is performed
via two different paths:
Path 1: A slow, quasi-static expansion where the external pressure is gradually reduced so that it is always
infinitesimally smaller than the gas pressure.
Path 2: A sudden expansion where the external pressure is instantaneously dropped to and kept constant
until the gas reaches equilibrium.
Consider the following statements:
(I) The change in internal energy of the gas is identical for both paths and is equal to zero.
(II) The work done by the gas in Path 1 is strictly greater than the work done by the gas in Path 2.
(III) The heat absorbed by the gas from the reservoir is greater in Path 2 than in Path 1 to compensate for the
energy dissipated due to irreversibility.
(IV) During Path 2, the gas passes through intermediate states where macroscopic properties like pressure and
temperature are not uniformly defined throughout its volume.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) (I) and (II) only (b) (I), (II) and (IV) only
(c) (I), (III) and (IV) only (d) (II), (III) and (IV) only

dynamic lift (Magnus force), causing its trajectory to curve downwards more sharply than that of an identical

(d) (A) is false but (R) is true

questions.question:
Assertion (A): For a particle executing simple harmonic motion, the frequency of oscillation of its kinetic
energy is double the frequency of its displacement, and its average kinetic energy over one complete time
period of displacement is exactly half of the total mechanical energy.
Reason (R): The kinetic energy is proportional to the square of the instantaneous velocity, which introduces a
squared trigonometric function of time; this mathematically doubles the angular frequency of the energy
oscillation and has a time-averaged value of over one complete cycle of displacement.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(c) (A) is true but (R) is false
(d) (A) is false but (R) is true

Assertion (A): The projection of a particle executing uniform circular motion on any diameter of its circular
path represents simple harmonic motion.
Reason (R): The component of the centripetal force acting on the particle along that diameter acts as a
restoring force for the projection, which is directly proportional to the displacement of the projection from the
center.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(c) (A) is true but (R) is false
(d) (A) is false but (R) is true

questions.question:
Assertion (A): When a point charge is placed inside a cavity of an uncharged isolated conductor, the net
electric field in the region outside the conductor is zero.
Reason (R): The phenomenon of electrostatic shielding ensures that the electric field of the charge placed
inside the cavity is completely blocked by the conductor and does not penetrate to the outside region.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(c) (A) is true but (R) is false
(d) (A) is false but (R) is true

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, interchanging the positions of the battery and the
galvanometer does not disturb the zero-deflection state of the galvanometer.
Reason (R): Kirchhoff's loop equations for the bridge network reveal that the condition for zero current in the
detector branch is the equality of the products of opposite arm resistances, a condition that remains
mathematically invariant upon swapping the source and detector terminals.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(c) (A) is true but (R) is false
(d) (A) is false but (R) is true

Consider the following statements regarding the internal resistance of a chemical cell:
(I) The internal resistance of a cell increases as the separation distance between its electrodes increases.
(II) The internal resistance of a cell is directly proportional to the area of the electrodes immersed in the
electrolyte.
(III) An increase in the temperature of the electrolyte leads to a decrease in the internal resistance of the cell.
(IV) The internal resistance of a cell is completely independent of the concentration of the electrolyte.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) (I) and (III) only (b) (II) and (IV) only
(c) (I), (II) and (IV) only (d) (III) and (IV) only

questions.question:
Assertion (A): If a charged particle moves in a region containing a spatially uniform but time-varying
magnetic field , its kinetic energy must remain constant.
Reason (R): The magnetic force acting on a charged particle is always perpendicular to its
instantaneous velocity vector , hence the work done by the magnetic force is zero.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(c) (A) is true but (R) is false
(d) (A) is false but (R) is true

paramagnetic state.
Reason (R): At temperatures above , the thermal agitation energy overcomes the exchange coupling
between atomic dipoles, destroying the parallel alignment within the magnetic domains.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(c) (A) is true but (R) is false
(d) (A) is false but (R) is true

C). Setup A shows the field lines around a bar magnet, while Setups B and C show the field lines when
spherical materials are placed in an initially uniform external magnetic field.
(I) In Setup A, the magnetic field lines form continuous closed loops, being directed from the South pole to
the North pole inside the magnet.
(II) The material in Setup B has a relative permeability , which is characteristic of a diamagnetic
substance.
(III) The material in Setup C strongly concentrates the magnetic field lines, indicating it is a ferromagnetic
substance with a large negative magnetic susceptibility ( ).
(IV) The magnetic field lines of a steady current-carrying finite solenoid are fundamentally different from
Setup A because they do not form continuous closed loops.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) (I) and (II) only (b) (I), (II) and (IV) only

secondary voltage is higher than the primary voltage.

(a) (I) and (II) only (b) (III) and (IV) only
(c) (I), (III) and (IV) only (d) (II) and (IV) only

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In a series circuit connected to an AC source, if the inductive reactance is greater than
the capacitive reactance, the applied voltage leads the current.
Reason (R): When the inductive reactance exceeds the capacitive reactance, the net reactance is inductive,
making the circuit behave predominantly like an circuit in which the current reaches its peak value earlier
than the applied voltage.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
(a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(c) (A) is true but (R) is false
(d) (A) is false but (R) is true
